answer: A mirror ledger stops cheap clones. Before a new key can earn, it must publish a lantern: one unique answer bound to a single address, readable by every peer. An atlas of earlier answers rejects any text that matches an older one. An attacker who wants many identities must write and publish a distinct lantern for each, then wait for established peers to attest that exact key. Copying one answer into ten keys fails the atlas, so the cost rises with every fake instead of staying flat.
